title: Design decision sets with assumptions and failure signals
summary: Write docs/design/decision-sets.md (no code): typed decision fields, sets by scope applied to role briefs, per-decision assumptions and failure signals that put a decision under review, fit with defaults-loop and Jev, and a migration plan for defaults.toml, D01-D90, addenda and job-record corrections.

defaults_applied.how: Design written with alternatives before any build.
Claims cite the repository files and decision numbers they rest on.
Hidden requirements recovered from BRIEF.md, defaults-loop.md, decisions.md.
Each proposed rule states its enforcement or is marked prose-only.

assumptions: Design only: no Rust, no schema files, no changes to defaults.toml or athena.toml.
Jev /v1/evaluate behavior is taken from what existing docs say; the producer reads defaults-loop.md and decisions.md first.
Decision numbering for any new decision recorded follows the next free D-number in docs/decisions.md.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/decision-sets.md exists and contains no code changes elsewhere; only docs files change.

Defines typed fields: kind (requirement, expectation, design, process), scope (classes of work, paths, phase: reading, producing, verifying, landing), status (active, proposed, superseded by a named decision), source, enforcement (code check, brief, prose only).

Explains grouping decisions into sets by scope and how a matching job's active decisions are applied to a role's brief like defaults are now, with defaults as one kind of decision, and how the token budget of the brief is respected.

Specifies per-decision assumptions and observable signals (rejections, interventions, corrections, check failures, host errors), how Athena watches them in records, and that a firing signal puts the decision under review rather than leaving it applied; uses D87 and the HTTP 405 merge refusal as the worked example.
Explains the fit with docs/design/defaults-loop.md (introspection step) and Jev /v1/evaluate for set membership and signal matching, citing what those files say.

Includes a migration section covering BRIEF.md addenda, defaults.toml's 12 defaults, docs/decisions.md D01-D90 including prose-only supersessions, and corrections in job records; lists alternatives considered and is concise.
Run cargo test and cargo fmt --check; both pass unchanged, confirming no code was altered.

out_of_scope: Implementing the decision store, matcher, or signal watcher
Actually migrating D01-D90 into typed records
Changing defaults.toml or any governance file
departures: A long design doc reading several large files costs somewhat more than the reference median.
